angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 633,783 km at 122.09 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.1908 +/- 0.0153 mas (same row, RUWE 1.23): 122.09 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.911 +/- 0.038 solar radii from Vach et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TIC 88785435 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..131V/abstract): 633,783 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.724 +/- 0.017 solar masses from Vach et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TIC 88785435 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..131V/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3998 +/- 95 K from Vach et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TIC 88785435 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..131V/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Vach et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TIC 88785435 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..131V/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/tic-88785435.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.379, rounded to two decimals
